anomalies.observed: On the root sheet the AVR-ISP header J4 carries global labels MISO on pin 1 and MOSI on pin 4, but these net names appear nowhere else. The microcontroller's ISP pins PB0 (pin 5) and PB1 (pin 6) are instead on nets named SDA and PWM (matching the I2C header J1 and the fan PWM drive). Only SCK (pin 7/PB2) and RST (pin 1/PB5) share a name with J4, so the header's data lines are dangling single-pin nets.
anomalies.expected: For an AVR-ISP header to function, MISO must be on the same net as the MCU's PB0 and MOSI on the same net as PB1 (the same physical pins also used as SDA/PWM). The MISO and MOSI nets should therefore be merged with the SDA and PWM nets, respectively, so the chip can be programmed.

evidence.quote: J4 'AVR-ISP-6' pin labels: MISO, MOSI, SCK, RST (root sheet, centre-bottom)
U2 ATtiny45-20P / U3 ATtiny13V-10S pin 5 = SDA, pin 6 = PWM (root sheet right and sheet 1/1 left)

anomalies.impact: The board cannot be programmed or debugged through J4: the MISO and MOSI header pins are not connected to the MCU, so in-system programming fails (and there is no other programming header, since J1 exposes only SDA/SCK/RST). The fan-control function itself still works via the matched SCK/RST/SDA/PWM nets.

parsed.summary: The fan-control circuitry (PMOS high-side switch, POT/TACH/I2C/PWM nets, regulator and decoupling) is internally consistent, but the AVR-ISP header J4's MISO and MOSI pins sit on nets that are not connected to the MCU's PB0/PB1 (which are named SDA/PWM), leaving the programming data lines open. This is a connectivity deviation from sound practice and is reported as the anomaly.
